title: Evaluation sections cover a split monic tensor algebra
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, I a finite index type and P_i in R[T] monic split polynomials. Set C to the tensor product of AdjoinRoot(P_i) as in [lem-weil-pbc-monic-tensor-presentation]. There exist a natural number n and surjective R-algebra homomorphisms e_k:C -> R (k in Fin n) such that every prime q of C is the inverse image under some e_k of a prime of R [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. In particular their spectral closed sections cover Spec C. No reducedness, domain or distinct-root hypothesis on R or P_i is imposed.

proof.text: Write each split monic P_i as the product of a finite multiset of linear factors. Index a finite family by all tuples of factors. Evaluating at the corresponding roots gives an R-algebra map e:C -> R by the tensor presentation map, and e is surjective because it is the identity on structural scalars.

For any prime q of C, pass to the domain quotient C/q. The image of each distinguished root satisfies P_i, so the product of its differences from the scalar roots is zero. The domain property gives one vanishing factor for each i; choose these factors to obtain a tuple k.

The quotient map C -> C/q agrees with C -> R -> C/q defined by e_k on the distinguished root of every tensor factor. Extensionality for AdjoinRoot and for finite tensor algebra maps proves equality everywhere. Taking kernels shows q = e_k^{-1}(q contracted to R), which is the asserted spectrum equality. Reindex the finite tuple type by Fin n. If it is empty the assertion is vacuous; for empty I it is a singleton.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_cover (R : Type u) [CommRing R] {ι : Type v} [Finite ι]
    (P : ι → R[X]) (hP : ∀ i, (P i).Monic) (hsp : ∀ i, (P i).Splits) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n → Tensor P →ₐ[R] R),
      (∀ k, Function.Surjective (e k)) ∧
      ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (Tensor P),
        ∃ (k : Fin n) (r : PrimeSpectrum R), PrimeSpectrum.comap (e k) r = q
